newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian decree sees household service rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Russian decree sees household service rate rise.

text.p: Russian households, which pay rates for electricity and household services that are under cost, will see their bills rise to close that gap by 2003 under a new presidential decree signed on Monday.

Household rates for all services -- set at 35 percent of cost in 1997 --will rise to 50 percent in 1998 and then climb by 10 percent increments until 2003, when rates will make up 100 percent of cost, the decree said.
First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov told a news conference that the reform would not hurt average Russians, in large part because average family expenditures would be capped.

Expenditures will be limited to 16 percent of total family expenditures in 1997, rising one to two percent per year until 2003, when families will pay no more than 25 percent of income on communal services, according to the decree.
